items.title: E1. Bradley–Terry and DPO by hand
items.prompt: Compute $\sigma(\Delta)$ for $\Delta\in\{0.5,1,2,4\}$ and recover the logit associated with a 75% win rate. Then evaluate two DPO pairs at $\beta=0.1$. The policy sequence log probabilities are $(-12.0,-11.5)$ for both pairs. The reference values are $(-13.0,-10.8)$ for pair I and $(-12.8,-11.65)$ for pair II. The preferred completion is listed first.
items.answer:
*Solution.* The sigmoid values are 0.622459, 0.731059, 0.880797, and 0.982014. The inverse logit is $\log(0.75/0.25)=\log3=1.098612$.

For pair I, policy chosen-minus-rejected margin is $-12-(-11.5)=-0.5$ and reference margin is $-13-(-10.8)=-2.2$. Their difference is 1.7, so $z=0.1\cdot1.7=0.17$ and $L=-\log\sigma(z)=0.611755$. For pair II, reference margin is $-12.8-(-11.65)=-1.15$; the margin gap is 0.65, giving $z=0.065$ and $L=0.661175$.

The derivative sign matters: $dL/dz=\sigma(z)-1$, so the values are **−0.457602** and **−0.483756**. At $\beta=0.5$, pair I has $z=0.85$, loss 0.355865, and $dL/dz=-0.299433$. The full parameter gradient also contains $\beta$ and log-probability derivatives.

items.title: E2. GRPO group and persistent-state memory
items.prompt: For rewards `[1,0,0,1,0,0,1,0]`, compute population-standardized advantages and the probability of a degenerate group of size 8 when the independent success probability is 0.3. Then compare the teaching PPO and DPO memory models for 8.03B parameters using 16 bytes per trainable parameter and 2 bytes per frozen bf16 parameter.
items.answer:
*Solution.* Three of eight rewards equal one, so $\mu=3/8=0.375$ and population standard deviation is $\sqrt{\frac18\sum_i(r_i-\mu)^2}=0.484123$. Standardization gives 1.290994 to successes and −0.774597 to failures; advantages sum to zero. A group is degenerate if all samples succeed or all fail: $0.3^8+0.7^8=0.057714$.

For 8.03B parameters, trainable state is $(8.03\cdot10^9\cdot16)/2^{30}\approx119.656$ GiB and a frozen bf16 copy is $(8.03\cdot10^9\cdot2)/2^{30}\approx14.957$ GiB. The teaching PPO anatomy has two trainable networks (policy and value) plus two frozen ones (reference and reward), giving $36\cdot8.03\cdot10^9/2^{30}\approx269.227$ GiB. DPO has one trainable policy plus one frozen reference, giving 134.613 GiB. These are persistent-state floors without activations or rollout buffers.

items.title: E3. Rollout economics
items.prompt: Generate 8 completions of 4,000 tokens for each of 256 prompts. Estimate generation time on eight accelerators at 209.4 tokens/s each. Compare it with a $6ND$ training estimate for an 8.03B model at 990 TFLOP/s per accelerator and 40% MFU.
items.answer:
*Solution.* Rollout volume is $D=256\cdot8\cdot4000=8{,}192{,}000$ tokens. Eight devices provide aggregate rate $8\cdot209.4=1675.2$ tok/s, so generation takes $D/1675.2=4890.2$ s = **81.50 minutes**.

Training arithmetic is

$$
C=6ND=6\cdot8.03\text{B}\cdot8.192\text{M}\approx3.946\cdot10^{17}\ \text{FLOP}.
$$

Effective throughput is $8\cdot990\text{ TFLOP/s}\cdot0.4=3.168\cdot10^{15}$ FLOP/s, hence 124.6 s = **2.076 minutes**. The ratio is 39.25: autoregressive rollout, not one training pass, dominates this scenario. It is not a universal RLVR constant.

items.title: E4 [project]
items.prompt:
Compare `run_dpo` at $\beta=0.1$ and $\beta=0.5$ using the same pairs and 140 updates. Begin with the default zero initialization, which makes both runs deterministic. Then set `init_std=0.02` and repeat the comparison for seeds 41, 42 and 43. Within each seed, both $\beta$ values must start from identical weights and an identical reference copied from those weights.


Record initial and final loss, training-pair ordering accuracy, held-out correct-answer probability and reference KL. Explain why losses measured at different $\beta$ values are not a direct scale of answer quality, and why correct training-pair ordering does not establish generation quality. As an optional extension, use an open 0.5–3B model with pinned templates and masks, then inspect response lengths and 50 generated answers.
